simple.meaning: חָרוּל (chârûwl) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, pointed , i.e. a bramble or other thorny weed.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חָרוּל (H2738) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 30:7, with occurrences in Job, Proverbs, Zephaniah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָרוּל (H2738) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חָרוּל (H2738) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חָרוּל (chârûwl) / H2738 is traced through Job 30:7, Proverbs 24:31, Zephaniah 2:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: Behold, it was all grown over with thorns.

definitions.short: properly, pointed , i.e. a bramble or other thorny weed
definitions.full: H2738. charul חָרוּל noun [masculine] a kind of weed, perhaps chickpea ( cicercula ), see Löw p. 153 (Syriac fodder for horses ; ᵑ7 Prov 24:31 gives חוּרְלָא ) — absolute ׳ח Job 30:6 ; Zeph 2:9 ; plural חֲרֻלִים Prov 24:31 ; — as growing in devastated land, collective Zeph 2:9 ; in vineyard of slothful, plural ח פניו ׳כִּסּוּ Prov 24:31 (|| קִמְּשׂגִים ); as sole shelter of certain outcast peoples Job 30:7 ( שִׂיחִים ).
definitions.rootNote: or (shortened) חָרֻל ; apparently, a passive participle of an unused root probably meaning to be prickly;
